nodes.result: AI-Researcher — a fully autonomous multi-agent system that orchestrates the complete scientific research pipeline from literature review and hypothesis generation through algorithm implementation, experimental validation, and publication-ready manuscript preparation with minimal human intervention.

nodes.result: Leading LLM-based agents achieve only 0.5% success on complete, executable AI research experiments; individual phases reach at most 20–35%, with key failure modes being experimental design misclassification (16.1%), missing implementation components (39.7%), and environment or dependency misconfiguration (29.4%).

nodes.result: OpenLens AI — a modular, fully automated research agent framework for health informatics — integrates specialized agents for literature review, data analysis, code generation, and manuscript preparation into an end-to-end pipeline that requires no human intervention.

nodes.result: ResearchGym — an extensible execution environment and benchmark of five containerized tasks (39 sub-tasks) derived from recent oral/spotlight papers at ICML, ICLR, and ACL — enables objective, execution-based evaluation of AI agents on closed-loop research, including hypothesis generation, experimentation, and surpassing human baselines, while remaining feasible on a single GPU.

nodes.label: Recurring long-horizon failure modes in autonomous research agents include impatience, poor time and resource management
nodes.result: Recurring long-horizon failure modes in autonomous research agents include impatience, poor time and resource management, overconfidence in weak hypotheses, difficulty coordinating parallel experiments, and context-length limits, as identified through ablations, 35+ end-to-end runs, and qualitative case studies.
nodes.paper: ResearchGym: Evaluating Language Model Agents on Real-World AI Research

nodes.result: AIRA_2 — an AI research agent combining asynchronous multi-GPU execution, Hidden Consistent Evaluation, and ReAct operators — achieves a mean Percentile Rank of 81.5% at 24 hours and 83.1% at 72 hours on MLE-bench-30, outperforming the strongest prior baseline (72.7%), and exceeds human state-of-the-art on 6 of 20 tasks on AIRS-Bench.

nodes.paper: AIRA_2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents

nodes.result: Hidden Consistent Evaluation (HCE) — standardizing data splits once across all candidates, hiding evaluation labels from the agent, and decoupling the search signal from the final selection signal — eliminates validation-test divergence and enables continued performance gains over extended (72-hour) search horizons.
nodes.paper: AIRA_2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents

nodes.result: Replacing fixed single-turn LLM operators with ReAct agents that autonomously scope exploratory data analysis, iterative debugging, and log inspection removes the operator-capability ceiling in agentic research systems, improving performance and accelerating discovery of strong solutions.
nodes.paper: AIRA_2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents

nodes.result: The performance degradation attributed to 'overfitting' in prior AI research agents over extended search horizons is caused by evaluation noise rather than true data memorization, as confirmed by ablation studies isolating the effect of evaluation consistency.
nodes.paper: AIRA_2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents
